simple.meaning: אֲרִאֵיל (ʼăriʼêyl) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the altar of the temple.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezekiel 43:15. The surrounding context includes altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲרִאֵיל (H741) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H741. ariel אֲרִאֵיל noun [masculine] hearth, altar-hearth ( ᵐ5 Ἀριηλ ; from ארה with ל aff. according to Ew § 163 g Ol § 220 Sm Ezek 43:15 Di Isa 29:1 and elsewhere; but this formation very rare & here dubious; ᵑ7 Hi De Brd Or 29:1 derive from אל + ארי = hearth of El , see also RS Semitic i. 469 , who thinks of pillar-altars; compare אראלדודה MI 12 see Sm & So, and Dr Sm xci ) — אראיל Kt Ezek 43:15-16 , (Qr אֲרִיאֵל ); = הַרְאֵל 43:15 (Vrss Co אריאל ), all with article, — of altar-hearth in Ezekiel's temple.
